header:
Date: 2025-10-21
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Liu (Redwood SE), Olivia Torres (Redwood CSM), Connor Lee (Redwood SE), Jamie Ortiz (Polaris Head of ML Ops), Rohit Patel (Polaris Infra), Lara Chen (Polaris Procurement), Sam Nguyen (Polaris Security)
summary: Quarterly renewal and expansion check-in. Polaris interested in moving more workload to Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) and adding eu-west-1 region for GDPR/data residency. Discussed pricing tiers, SLA expectations, SOC 2/KMS/VPC requirements, benchmark plan, and contract extension options. Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmarks, security docs, and draft addendum.
topics: Dedicated capacity pricing and commit levels
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is the renewal / expansion check-in for Polaris Health - we wanted to go over capacity, regions, and next steps. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Jamie Ortiz: Pretty good, thanks. Busy but good. Appreciate the time.
[00:12] Rohit Patel: Hey, quick note i'm on mobile so audio may be meh.
[00:15] Ethan Park: no worries. Quick agenda: renewal term options, dedicated capacity pricing, eu-west-1 availability, security items Sam had, and benchmarks. Maya will cover perf questions.
[00:26] Maya Liu: hi all — i'll run through a short perf/arch recap then we can talk numbers.
[00:31] Sam Nguyen: thanks. quick ask from security side: we need SOC 2 latest report, network diagram, and confirmation on KMS/HSM options for keys. also, any EU data residency guarantees?
[00:44] Ethan Park: yes, we can share SOC 2 right after this. KMS integrations are supported — we have both customer-managed KMS and HSM options for Private deployments; for Dedicated we support CMEK with our KMS connectors, and for Hosted we also support bring-your-own-key in private deployments, i might be mixing terms — but we'll send the doc.
[01:02] Jamie Ortiz: great. On the capacity side, our usage has grown 2.7x q/q. Current hosted plan is struggling on peak times, and the team is pushing for dedicated GPUs in eu-west-1 to keep latency to users in EU. What's realistic timeline?
[01:20] Olivia Torres: from the CSM side, we've seen small customers go live in a couple weeks once contracts and infra are set, but provisioning dedicated pools typically takes 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and region availability.
[01:30] Connor Lee: To add, eu-west-1 has constraints sometimes, we can prioritize your pool and give you a lead time estimate once you commit to a sizing tier.
[01:40] Rohit Patel: what's the sizing tiers look like? We're thinking 4-8 GPUs to start, with burst to 12 if needed. Also need predictable throughput and an SLA for p99 latency.
[01:51] Maya Liu: Typical tiers: small (4xA10-like), medium (8xA100-ish), large (16+). Pricing and perf vary of course; we'll attach the recommended quant profiles. For p99 we can discuss target numbers — depends on model and seq length, but we support canary rollouts and fallback to smaller models to preserve SLA.
[02:12] Jamie Ortiz: fallback policies are useful. Also curious about caching — prefix caching or KV cash? we want to make sure we're not paying for repeated context.
[02:21] Maya Liu: KV cache — yes we do KV cache and prefix caching for commonly repeated prompts. That usually reduces token cost on stable prompts substantially. There was some transcription note: sometimes 'KV cash' in older docs, lol.
[02:33] Lara Chen: from procurement: pricing is the core ask. Also, if we extend term to 24 months, what's the discount bucket?
[02:41] Ethan Park: good question. Our standard committed tiers have volume discounts: 12 month, 18 month, 24 month — discount increases with term and committed GPU-hours. For example, 24-month commit often gets an additional 7-12% off base dedicated rates plus prioritized region placement. I'll send concrete numbers after this call.
[02:58] Rohit Patel: can you scope out the cost delta between hosting in us-east-1 vs eu-west-1? inc tax/regulatory costs too.
[03:07] Ethan Park: yes — eu regions are slightly higher due to infra costs and egress, we will break down per-token and per-hour costs in the quote.
[03:15] Sam Nguyen: also need to confirm audit logs retention and SAML/SSO options, RBAC model, and that we can integrate with our SIEM for log forwarding.
[03:25] Maya Liu: audit logs are available; retention is configurable as an add-on. We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and syslog/CloudWatch forwarding. We'll include the integration doc link.
[03:37] Jamie Ortiz: what's the plan for benchmarks? we want to see p50/p95/p99 latency numbers for our gen workloads in eu-west-1.
[03:44] Maya Liu: we can run a benchmark using your representative prompt set. Ideally we get a subset of prompts and expected seq lengths. Proposed plan: you share prompts (sanitized), we run in a dedicated eu-west-1 pool with the model variants you use, measure latency and token cost over a 2-hour simulation.
[04:00] Rohit Patel: timeline?
[04:02] Maya Liu: we can schedule next week — quickest run would be 2 business days after we have the prompt set and access. I'll coordinate with your infra team.
[04:10] Ethan Park: note on compatibility: if you need private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for regulatory reasons we can offer that as part of Private plan; Dedicated is isolated but still managed. We'll clarify options in the doc.
[04:21] Sam Nguyen: for EU PHI concerns, we might need Private deployment or strict data flow controls. Can you confirm that dedicated pools don't persist raw prompts beyond session requirements and that audit logs don't contain raw PHI?
[04:33] Connor Lee: short answer: we have configurable redaction and retention policies; default behavior is to not retain model inputs beyond cached prefixes or KV where configured, and you can opt for no-persist mode on certain routes. We'll send specifics.
[04:46] Jamie Ortiz: excellent. Quick question from product: what about model variants and quantization? can we get a slightly cheaper footprint with int8 without quality loss?
[04:56] Maya Liu: yes, we provide recommended quant profiles per model; for many workloads int8 or 4-bit quant gives up to 2-4x memory savings with minimal quality regression. Our Optimize team runs evals; we'll include suggested candidates for your prompt set in the benchmark.
[05:10] Lara Chen: procurement asks for a contract addendum template for extending to 24 months and adding eu-west-1 capacity. Can you provide a draft?
[05:18] Olivia Torres: yes — i'll draft an addendum with the tier, term, and SLA points and circulate.
[05:23] Rohit Patel: is there a kill-switch or capacity fallback if a region becomes saturated? We don't want downtime.
[05:30] Ethan Park: we have smart routing and automated fallback to compatible model variants or cross-region failover; for Dedicated you can specify burst to other regions or fallback hosted capacity. We'll show the routing policy options in the doc.
[05:42] Jamie Ortiz: any caveats about telemetry and cost visibility? we need token-level cost breakdowns so finance can reconcile spend.
[05:50] Connor Lee: Console has per-token cost and latency breakdown, per-route dashboards, and we can provide raw usage exports for your FinOps tooling. That's in the observability add-on.
[05:59] Jamie Ortiz: what about support SLAs for enterprise?
[06:03] Ethan Park: Reserved capacity customers get 24/7 support with a 1-hour P1 response on higher tiers; we can map that to contract.
[06:10] Sam Nguyen: does the SLA cover model quality regressions? we need rollback tools for rollouts if output quality drops after a model swap.
[06:18] Maya Liu: yes, rollouts include automatic rollback policies and canary gating with quality metrics; the console can tie evals to prompt sets to trigger alerts.
[06:26] Jamie Ortiz: ok, rough asks captured: pricing for 4/8/12 GPU tiers in eu-west-1, discount options for 24-month commit, SOC2 and network docs, benchmark plan and times, contract addendum. Anything else?
[06:38] Lara Chen: please include the pricing for observability retention add-on and what logs are included.
[06:43] Ethan Park: will do.
[06:45] Maya Liu: quick note — for benchmarking we may need a small test token key for a dedicated test instance, we'll request a service account and temporary access.
[06:55] Rohit Patel: fine, security will set it up. Sam will coordinate.
[07:00] Sam Nguyen: yep i'll send the access details.
[07:03] Ethan Park: perfect. Let's recap next steps.
[07:06] Olivia Torres: recap: Ethan will send updated pricing and region cost breakdown, Maya will run benchmarks in eu-west-1 once prompts are shared, Olivia will draft addendum, Sam (Polaris) will share SOC2 and security answers, Lara will confirm renewal term by 2025-10-28.
[07:20] Jamie Ortiz: sounds good. Any blockers?
[07:23] Rohit Patel: none immediate — need the pricing and benchmark results to proceed.
[07:27] Ethan Park: ok everyone's clear. we'll target to have the quote and initial docs to you by Friday (2025-10-24).
[07:34] Lara Chen: good. thanks all.
[07:36] Ethan Park: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and the SOC pack. Bye.
